# Jeremiah 31 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** "At-that time," declares YHWH, "I-will-be God to-all [the]-families-of Israel, and-they will-be to-Me for-a-people."

**2** Thus says YHWH: "Found grace in-the-wilderness — a-people [who were]-survivors-of [the]-sword; going to-find-his-rest — Israel."

**3** From-afar YHWH appeared to-me: "And-[with]-an-everlasting love I-loved-you; therefore I-drew-you [with]-lovingkindness.

**4** Again I-will-build-you and-you-will-be-built, virgin Israel; again you-will-adorn-yourself [with]-your-tambourines and-go-forth in-[the]-dance-of the-merrymakers.

**5** Again you-will-plant vineyards on-[the]-mountains-of Samaria; [the]-planters will-plant and-will-enjoy-[the]-fruit.

**6** For there-will-be a-day [when]-watchmen will-call on-[the]-hill-country-of Ephraim: 'Arise, and-let-us-go-up to-Zion, to YHWH our-God!'"

**7** And-YHWH spoke concerning the-restoration-of Israel and-the-gathering from-all the-nations where He-scattered-them.

**31** "Behold, days are-coming," declares YHWH, "and-I-will-cut with-[the]-house-of Israel and-with-[the]-house-of Judah a-covenant new.

**32** Not like-the-covenant which I-cut with-their-fathers in-the-day I-took-hold-of their-hand to-bring-them-out from-[the]-land-of Egypt, which they broke — My-covenant — and-I was-a-husband to-them," declares YHWH.

**33** "For this [is] the-covenant which I-will-cut with-[the]-house-of Israel after those days," declares YHWH: "I-will-put My-law in-their-inward-parts, and-upon their-heart I-will-write-it; and-I-will-be to-them for-God, and-they will-be to-Me for-a-people.

**34** And-they-will-not teach again each his-neighbor and-each his-brother, saying, 'Know YHWH,' for all-of-them will-know-Me, from-their-least to-their-greatest," declares YHWH, "for I-will-forgive their-iniquity, and-their-sin I-will-not-remember again."

**35** And-YHWH declared the-permanence-of His-covenant, like-the-fixed-order-of sun and-moon and-stars.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **31:3**: Ahavat olam — 'an everlasting love.' The eternal nature of God's love grounds the restoration promise in divine character, not human merit.

- **31:31-34**: Berit chadashah — 'new covenant.' The only occurrence of this exact phrase in the Hebrew Bible. The 'newness' lies in internalization: Torah written on hearts, not tablets.

- **31:33**: Be-qirbam — 'in their inward parts.' The contrast with external stone tablets is deliberate. The new covenant transforms the locus of divine instruction from external to internal.

— EMET
